# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-148 @ `aea410c`, TIER 1) | **NO GO — found that the incident message this feature EXISTS to show is destroyed 12 ms after it is written, on every path including token-still-live; proved it in a real browser it stood up itself** (2026-09-07 19:07) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Wednesday raised this from the queue tail to tier 1 and the gate justified it. **It solved the drivability constraint rather than reporting it** — stood the app up locally from that commit (port 3099, fresh empty `DATA_DIR`, Chromium/Playwright) and produced a **MutationObserver timeline**: status "" → "Revoking token…" → **"" at t+12 ms**, with the server on the same click returning 500 and `scimTokenConfigured=true` — **the token still live and the page byte-identical to before the click.** Positive control: the success path blanks identically, so the blank is not a failed request. **The keeper: it diagnosed why the SHIPPED TEST stayed green** — the fixture injects `#rd135-status` as a sibling OUTSIDE the container `render()` wipes (real page 1 node inside → ""; fixture 2 nodes outside → full warning) — **and noted the test file's own header cites that exact defect class, so it committed the thing it was written to guard.** Also found the file's own sibling handlers all call `render()` before `setStatus()`, so the fix is the file's existing pattern; counted **17 `confirm()` guards for milder controls** to ground F-3. Explicitly credited the server half as well built. |
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-329 @ `2e78c76`, TIER 2 through-code) | **GO-with-findings — 6 tamper classes caught, 10 MISSED, each proved on the wire from a booted server; and it found the stronger instrument was already in the next file** (2026-09-07 18:54) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Applied Wednesday's standing line exactly — *narrow, not fake, hence GO-with-findings*. **F-2 is the keeper: the "belt-and-braces" deny-list is NOT a second layer** — it shares the allow-list's parser; on tamper E `nodeVersion` is ON the deny-list, went out on the wire, and **both cells stayed green**. *"Two layers that fail together are one layer"* — and the commit message presents them as independent. **The one thing it would change:** the builder's note called source-reading "the strongest instrument available without booting the app" — true as worded, **but this repo ALREADY boots the app** (`__tests__/erasure-health-branches.test.js:97-143` spawns the real server on a reserved port); rebuilt on that pattern it **caught 7 of the 10 misses.** Ten misses each `node --check` clean and read off the wire, incl. a full spread leaking `persistence.dataDir`, an allowed KEY with a sensitive VALUE, and two keys on one physical line defeating a line-anchored regex. **Credited the builder honestly:** its CONTROL asserts the tamper landed BEFORE asserting the effect — the check RD-362's control lacked — and named L and N as limits of BOTH instruments, not just the builder's. |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-969 item 1 / PR #892 @ `f54b2dce1`, TIER 2) | **NO GO on a BLOCKER: the fix REPRODUCED ITS OWN TICKET'S DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **F1:** on a machine without `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — **the normal state of a clean stack per KS-915, and the case the builder's OWN design note cites** — the step reports a green `PROVISIONED`, writes a manifest where **all five actors collapse to `OWNER`**, and **that manifest OUTRANKS the correctly-roled seeded accounts in every consumer.** So the PR switches every wired suite to wrongly-roled identities **by default and calls it succes

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
